newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny Teledyne metals unit profit up.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny Teledyne metals unit profit up.

text.p: Allegheny Teledyne Inc said Wednesday first quarter 1997 operating profit of its specialty metals unit improved 6.0 percent to $72.3 million compared to the same period in 1996, while sales rose 1.0 percent to $543.5 million.
Operating profit from businesses other than flat-rolled products doubled compared with the same period in 1996 with sales increasing 24 percent, it said.

"Our first quarter results for the specialty metals segment reflect the growth in our high-value metals businesses, which more than offset the lower prices in flat-rolled commodity stainless steel," said Richard P. Simmons, chairman, president and chief executive officer of the company.
Meanwhile, operating profits for the other three business segments -- aerospace-electronics, industrial, and consumer -- met or exceeded year-ago results, he said.
"We continue to take full advantage of the operating and financial synergies from the combination of Allegheny Ludlum and Teledyne, he said.
Operating cost savings improved further, and corporate expenses continued to decline. Further corporate expense reductions are expected through the balance of 1997, he added.
